page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.vgn6i-m16-vws.5xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. This configuration provides 20 dedicated vCPUs derived from 10 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 92.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.6 GB per core. Acceleration is provided by a single integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance is positioned in the lower tier, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10% to 25% categories. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth tests show average read and write speeds, although the Passmark memory score is relatively weak. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput all perform within the middle 50% benchmark range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a balanced entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads without the premium cost of high-end accelerators. The combination of a dedicated Intel Xeon CPU and an NVIDIA T4 GPU makes it suitable for workloads that benefit from GPU acceleration but do not require extreme single-core CPU performance. Appropriate workloads include entry-level machine learning inference, video transcoding, virtual workstations, and database operations that can leverage the GPU or the 20-vCPU multi-core capacity.
